text:
Base44 is being acquired by Wix.

There’s a lot I’d like to share - probably more than what fits in a post.

Here are some thoughts, in no particular order:

1. Crazy f***ing journey so far. 
I’m grateful to everyone who’s been part of it - and most importantly, to the incredible community that has come to be since launching this product a few months ago.

2. Wix is Base44’s natural partner. I know it sounds like a cliché every founder says when they’re acquired - but I genuinely believe in this case it’s 100% true.

Same product category, same vision, same DNA, same customer obsession. Many overlapping user profiles.

Given the similarities, the decision to join forces was easier than I expected. 
Still, not an easy one to make.

3. What’s behind this decision:
This market moves fast. Very, very fast.
We’re riding strong momentum - 
honestly, the best I’ve seen for a company at our stage, especially a bootstrapped one. 
The product bet Base44 made - building all-in-one (backend, authentication, integrations, etc.) - is paying off.

That being said - the scale and volume we need is not something we can organically grow into. 
At some point - after a few sleepless nights chatting with Avishai - I realized that joining forces with Wix is the best decision I can make for Base44 and its community. 

I believe Base44 has a real shot at building something truly transformative, global - 
a product that moves the needle for a lot of people and companies. 

It’s not going to be easy, and there’s still a long road ahead - but partnering with Wix, at exactly the right moment (this one), basically triples our chances of getting there.

4. What should you expect to change? 
Nothing too much. 
Better support, faster product velocity, and community will likely grow faster, increasing our b2b features. 

If we were able to get so far organically, bootstraped, I’m excited to see our new pace now that we have all the resources in place. 

I’ll share a post about our product roadmap in the next few days.

5. It’s day 1 for Base44.
The amount of love and support that Base44 and I received so far from the community has been unbelievable. 
I hope to be able to serve it even better given our new status.
We have everything we need to win - and the backing of the best possible partner.

text:
Base44 ended up making $189K profit in May, not $100K as expected.

What changed:

- Faster, unexpected growth
- Drastically reduced LLM costs (see graph below)

Sharing some details below on what helped improve margins:
---

Growth:

What worked - 
- Affiliate program is driving some traffic and revenue. 
- People are sharing their experiences building with Base44 more aggressively
- AWS summit keynote 
- B2B deals are taking off 🔥 - companies are buying bulk licenses for their product teams

What didn't work (yet) - 
Been experimenting a bit with meta ads. 
Still small numbers since ROI isn’t there yet, but I’m optimistic.
---

Cost:
To be honest, the main driver for the margins improvement is Claude 4.
Here's the breakdown:

1. Fewer bugs -
When there’s a bug in a user’s app, Base44 doesn’t charge credits - at least for most of the bugs (i.e. users press the "Resolve with AI" button).

It’s a good thing because it aligns incentives with the user, 
But it can get very expensive when the AI gets stuck in a loop.

Claude 4 is producing *significantly* fewer bugs.

The direct impact: fewer bugs -> lower costs ->  better margins.
The indirect impact: happier users -> lower churn.

2. Fewer LLM calls -
When users create an app, the first message is the most expensive — it generates a lot of code from scratch

Previously, I had to concatenate multiple LLM responses to generate a full working app from the first prompt.

Claude 4 has a 32k output window (vs. 16k on Sonnet 3.7), which means fewer requests and lower costs.

3. Prompt Caching:
There was a bug I didn’t notice that probably cost Base44 $20K–$30K.

The cache was set to 5 minutes by default, which is too short of a window. 
After increasing it to 1 hour, input token costs dropped.
----

What's ahead -
Feels like costs are pretty optimized for now.

The next big gains will likely come from:

- Improving and automating support
- And obviously — new growth strategies (app catalog is coming!)

*Can’t recommend them enough*. No need for extra DevOps work or headcount — it just works. Also comes in handy when someone tries to DDoS Base44 every now and then. 

Database – MongoDB. Super flexible, no painful migrations like you’d get with SQL.
Once you build enough infra on top, it’s very smooth to work with.
Early on I did run into some performance issues — mostly due to not understanding Mongo’s hosting tiers. (Tip: Don’t try scaling on shared/virtual CPUs.)

Emails – SendGrid. Pricey, I think it's worth it for now. I do want to test Resend soon.

Payments – Stripe. 
Still the easiest and most reliable option for SaaS. 
Downsides:
- Failed payments are a black box - hard to debug
- Disputes are very expensive

Models – Using a mix. 
Claude 3.7 is still the workhorse (via Bedrock, with fallback to Anthropic’s own API). 
But Gemini 2.5 Pro is catching up — I’ve seen it handle complex coding tasks with cleaner solutions. 

The interesting thing is that I’ve stopped using OpenAI through the API, finding much better alternatives via Bedrock (AWS) / Vertex (Google) / Anthropic.

Logging and observability - Logfire (by Pydantic) 
An up-and-coming alternative to Datadog. Much easier to use, and there's a great team behind it. So far I'm a happy customer.

—-

Operational Stack
Stripe Atlas – Set up the company through it. In my last startup, incorporation took weeks and $$$. Atlas is a game changer.

Brex – Love the product, makes managing finances effortless such that there's no need for a finance team (yet).

Cross-border payments are still very costly. I've tried setting up Wise to pay vendors outside of the US, but so far it has been more headache than help.

Community - Using Discord. Not sure I love it (maybe just a learning curve vs. Slack).

Internal Tools – I built everything else in Base44 itself:
- Docs
- User management
- Marketing content
- Coupon/credit system
- Hackathon coordination
- CRM for B2B deals

---

Three years ago my mom was diagnosed with cancer. She froze, and my family and I started hunting for answers. We hit mountains of information that didn’t fit, and when we found things that could really help, it was too late. 
Last year we lost her. 
From that horrible pain came the idea for a free app that gives cancer patients and their loved ones only the information and tools that really matter.

At the Base44 Hackathon alongside my talented teammates — 𝐈𝐟𝐚𝐭 𝐀𝐦𝐢𝐭 - יפעת עמית and Mor Zalkai, we turned that idea into SMADAR.

I’ve been a Product Manager for a while and have written plenty of features, but these are the features I’m proudest of:

• Role based flows – Patients, Caregivers, Doctors, Volunteers each get just the tools they need.
• Caregiver link with custom permissions – Patients choose exactly what a caregiver can see and do.
• Community Lounge – Live groups and forums for real-time support and shared tips.
• AI Chat – Explains medical terms in plain words and suggests next steps.
• Record & summarize visits – One tap records a doctor meeting and returns shareable action items.
• Smart Knowledge Hub – articles, clinical trials, financial/legal help, nutrition and mental-health content matched to the user’s exact diagnosis, stage and location.
• Treatment Companion – Step by step checklists for Before Treatment (prep, paperwork, what to bring), Treatment Day (where to go, who to meet, live reminders), and After Treatment (side effect tracker, recovery tips, follow up schedule).
• Volunteer Match – Need a ride for chemotherapy treatment? Nearby volunteers get a ping and can accept with one tap.
• Wellness Marketplace – A shop with discounted products and services that truly help patients feel better.
• Daily Health Challenges – Small goals with points and progress tracking to keep motivation high.

Huge thanks to Maor Shlomo for an amazing experience. Your mission to make the world a better place has been successfully accomplished - and we’re just getting started. ❤️

text:
Base44's Biggest Release to Date:  Backend Functions!

*You can now connect your Base44 app to any service, API, or database*.

This release allows a whole new class of apps to be built with Base44:

• Build apps that connect to your CRM.
• Integrate custom payment providers.
• Connect apps with your WhatsApp account.
• Integrate with your preferred LLM, text-to-speech, or image generation model.
• Connect to your organization's proprietary APIs and data.

And so much more!
----

How Does It Work?

• Go to your app's settings and click "Activate Backend Functions." 
• Ask Base44 to create a function (e.g., "enable the ability to export tasks to a PDF").
• If any API key or secret is needed, Base44 will prompt you before creating the function.
• Base44 will write the function and integrate it with the app.
• You can test and edit the function from the built-in code editor (Workspace → Code → Functions).

Backend functions comes with a set of tools to test, edit, and debug that can be found in the app's workspace.

----

Technical Details:
• Backend functions are JavaScript functions that run in a fast, scalable, and isolated environment (thanks to our friends at Deno).
• These functions can access any npm package by simply naming it in the import.
• They are deployed to a dedicated URL on every change, and your app can access these functions using the Base44 SDK.
• Functions can return any type of data—JSON, binary, etc.

----

Caveats:
• The experience is still far from where I want it to be. For those who are not technical, I'd recommend waiting a few days until this feature matures.
• LLMs are not yet great at memorizing APIs, so manual adjustments and fixes to the code might be needed.
• Occasionally, you'll need to explain to the LLM that your desired feature requires a backend function.

Currently available for Builder and above plans. I'll extend access as the capability matures. 
Eager to get some feedback!

text:
Building a SaaS alone -

Below is a *long* thread with lessons i learned starting Base44 solo - 

which turned out to be *very* different than my experience running a VC funded company, with multiple engineering teams.
---

1. Nobody cares how you build stuff. 

Nobody cares what programming language you’re using. What infrastructure do you use or whether you have a pretty CI/CD process in place. 
There would be no “this will not scale” debates that usually happen when working in teams. 

Just build stuff in whatever way is the easiest for you to build.

It’s most likely that your product will not find real usage way before you reach a point where infrastructure breaks because you took a bad decision.

2. on the flip side - There’s no on-call engineer and no QA to check that what you’re releasing right now won’t introduce severe bugs.

If you won’t build it right - either bad experience or your own personal stress will kill your business.

For Base44 - I’ve set up an infrastructure that works *for me*. 
It might be a nightmare for someone else. 

I push to production 13 times a day, deployment takes 7 minutes. 

Stability is definitely not perfect, but I feel like it’s better than competition. 
It’s a good enough to balance velocity without constant fear of breaking stuff as I build.  

—-

3. Brutal prioritisation  - 
When you’re solo (and bootstrapped), every single hour matters.
You need to get to profitability, and get there fast. 

First you'll have to ruthlessly prioritize what features you build and what markets you go after.

For example - I know there’s a huge market opportunity for letting people  build games with Base44. 

If i was heavily funded with a team of 50, by now there would a handful of engineers working on improving that aspect of Base44. There's not. 

Schedule 🗓️- 
One of the hardest thing to prioritise early on is your schedule. Who do you meet.

My advice for starting a bootstrapped business - 
For the first couple of months do not meet any person that is not a potential user who might turn eventually to a paid user.
---

4. Use AI heavily 
It’s impossible to get to a velocity that’s competitive enough in today’s market without using LLMs, and using it right. 

It will allow you to write many features. 
Most of them will not be used,
Some of them will, and it will be clear which ones are.
Delete the rest. 

Starting Base44, I almost deleted features at the same pace that i was  building them. 
Truth is, that  before you have hundreds of users, it’s really not that clear what you should build. 
And these days, 
the playbook of "validate everything before you build it" is irrelevant anymore -when it's so easy to build.
---

Lastly - 
5. Vanity Metrics - 
When you’re alone, metrics don’t matter. You don’t need to convince anybody to invest or join, 
Product engagement and product velocity is the only thing that matters. Everything else is a derivative of that.

text:
Yesterday, Base44 crossed 20k users and became profitable.

So I figured it’s as good a time as any to share some of my lessons, learnings and mistakes. 

Starting with the 0-> 1 part, or how I got my first couple of users - 

While there are many ways to start, 
and I’ve tried several of them throughout the years, 
here’s what I used for Base44 and what turned out to be my favorite:

👉 Build for a problem you understand better than anyone else.
👉 Find 3-5 people close to you who will live in your product daily.
--- 
Why a problem you know deeply?

Because it’s really easy to build software right now.
And it’s easy to come up with ideas that *should*, on paper, generate revenue. 

Ideas, and software, are easier to copy - than a true deep understanding of a field. 

Base44 is an idea I’ve obsessed over for years.
I’ve researched different ways of approaching it. I tried building MVPs throughout the years, all of them failed. 

Recently, LLMs finally made Base44 feasible, but only after years of deep research and failed attempts. 

--- 
Then comes the hardest part:

Your first users.

Sometimes I think it’s better to find the users before the problem.
Because it’s that hard.

You need 3-5 people who will gladly live inside your broken, unfinished, embarrassing v1.

How do you get them?
Start with friends or family.
People who want you to win.
People who’ll tolerate your buggy mess, give you feedback, and keep showing up.

For Base44, I started with 3 close friends.
Solo founders.
Non-technical.
All needing to build their business quickly - and implement a product vision they have in mind.


This is the cheat code:
Sit with them, physically.
Watch them struggle. See exactly where your product breaks.

Fix it. Repeat.

For now - Forget scaling. Forget distribution.
Just make something that solves their problem better each day.

I stayed in this phase until i knew that I had >= 1 "vitality coefficient". 
Meaning - that when i share the product with a new user, *on average*, this user will stay, use, and potentially introduce new users to the platform. 

*On average* is important here - many users will not stay. and that's ok!

Sometimes prompting the chat is not enough, and sometimes - you want to understand what's under the hood. 
Fast Code Edits is an in browser IDE that allows you to make instant code edits to your app's files.
To make iterations even faster - when previewing a page in your app,

Currently rolled out to all paid tiers.

continue with your favorite IDE, and deploy them easily on your own infrastructure. 
The integration is still in beta, and should be improved over the next couple of weeks.

Currently rolled out to builder and pro tiers.

text:
Excited to share a project I’ve been working on lately..

Base44 .com 

Base44 is a moonshot experiment - helping everyone, technical or not, build software without coding, at all. 

For the past decade or so - I’ve been obsessed with the idea of what possibilities will open up if everyone can build their own tools or apps - and lately it’s seemed feasible enough to take a shot at it.

It’s not the first tool aiming to allow people to build software using natural language, 
But we’re taking what I think is a very different and opinionated approach  -
Every app in Base44 is created with a built-in DB, storage layer, authentication, analytics and countless  integrations… or as our users like to call it -  "batteries included”.

This way - people can build happily without worrying what an API key means or how to set up this and that. 

Since launching ~3 weeks ago, we went from (almost) 0 users to over 10k,
And people are building genuinely incredible stuff. 
Some examples - 

Ron, former restaurant manager - is building a SaaS platform for restaurants to manage invoices and expenses. Signed his first couple of customers within 2 weeks 

René, South Africa, built a personal finance tracker app with AI-fused suggestions - and is growing every day with users from all over the world

Aravind (12!), US, has built his own version of a pokemon game. 

—-

Give it a shot and tell me how it went.
It’s been a blast watching people bring their ideas to life. I’d love to see what more people create with it.
